subject: Archaeology
title: Roman Medicine: Surgery Without Anesthesia
description: A 60-second lesson on Roman Medicine: Surgery Without Anesthesia.

hook.text: Roman surgeons performed cataract removal, skull drilling, and cesarean sections — without modern painkillers.

buildup.text: Bronze surgical kits found at Pompeii include scalpels, forceps, bone saws.

discovery.text: Military hospitals called valetudinaria were found at frontier forts — standardized wards with herb gardens for medicines.

twist.text: They used opium and henbane as anesthetics. Galen, Rome's greatest doctor, tested drugs on gladiators first.

climax.text: A healed skull from Roman Britain shows that a patient survived brain surgery — the bone grew back around the hole.

punchline.text: Roman doctors drilled skulls and patients survived.

quiz.question: What did archaeological finds at Roman frontier forts reveal?
options: Soldiers had no access to medical care and relied on folk remedies
Standardized military hospitals with wards and herb gardens for medicine
Only officers received medical treatment during military campaigns
